newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends down after UN gives Iraq green ligh.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends down after UN gives Iraq green ligh.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended down on Monday, but off lows with a dogged but fairly modest retracement of losses in the last few hours of trade.
Jan Brent ended 46 cents down at $24.08 a barrel, having dipped to a session low of $23.77 after U.N. gave the final go-ahead for Iraqi oil sales.
"We did pull back a little bit, but it was all pretty half-hearted. The volumes are thin," said one IPE floor broker.

U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Monday sent notification to the Security Council enabling the oil-for-food deal with Iraq to enter into force at 0501 GMT on Tuesday, a U.N. spokesman said.
But some brokers claimed that the impact of Iraqi oil was already discounted by the market and noted that seaborne exports aren't expected until January.
"No ships have as yet been chartered, so crudes may not hit the market as fast as implied," said Charles Gray of Prudential-Bache London futures brokers in his daily report.
Dealers said that Monday's move to the downside was more of a reaction to a sharp late rally on Friday than to the prospect of Iraqi oil sales.
"It climbed 50 cents in the last ten minutes on Friday so this is the correction you'd expect regardless of the headlines."
Brokers pegged support for Jan Brent at the session low of $23.77 a barrel and resistance at $24.25.
Dec gas oil closed $8.50 a tonne lower at $215.50, while Jan shed $7.50 to end the session at $216.50, allowing the front months to slip into contango ahead of Dec's expiry on Thursday.

Brokers said the end of strikes at Elf refineries in France, forecasts of moderate weather in the U.S., and talk of heavy buying on January by a Wall Street trader combined to push the market into contango for the first time since August.
Some suggested that the trading house which lifted the bulk of the record Nov delivery was selling heavy prompt spot volumes.
